fy.title: Williams - First-Year Admission (deadlines, checklist, test-optional policy, codes)

aid.title: Williams - Tuition & Aid: Requirements and Deadlines

test_policy.notes: Williams describes itself as truly test optional; SAT/ACT is superscored if submitted (including across legacy and enhanced ACT); ACT Science is optional. Applicants may change their mind about submitting before the deadline.

requirements.notes: Common App, Apply Coalition with Scoir, or QuestBridge. No required writing supplement (an academic writing sample is optional). Counselor letter plus two teacher letters; mid-year report due Feb 6. Williams does not conduct interviews (InitialView interviews may be shared). The pages do not give the entry year, so the dates are assumed to be for the fall 2027 cycle (the aid page references 2027-2028).

deadlines.label: Early Decision (binding)
deadlines.notes: Admission and financial aid applications are due at the same time. Page says decision 'by December 14'.

english_policy.waiver_notes: If English is not your first language or the language of academic instruction at your school, Williams encourages you to submit TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo scores (self-report, email a screenshot, or send from the testing agency). Scores of enrolling students are verified. No minimums are published; the figures below are the typical range of competitive applicants.

english.notes: Competitive applicants typically score 100-120 (taken before January 2026). Typical range, not a minimum.
Competitive applicants typically score 5-6 on the new scale. Typical range, not a minimum.
Competitive applicants typically score 7.5-9. Typical range, not a minimum.
Competitive applicants typically score 135-160. Typical range, not a minimum.

aid.notes: Not need-blind for international applicants, but aid meets 100% of demonstrated need, is guaranteed for all four years, and about 70% of international students receive aid (average award over $90,000). Applicants who may seek aid at any point must answer Yes to the aid question on the application; aid materials are requested only after admission. No merit scholarships are described.

tier_notes.humanities: Top liberal-arts humanities; small classes and tutorials.
tier_notes.arts_design: Art history program is a well-known pipeline to museums and graduate study.
